turns.question: Why is the rate variance threshold set at 15%?

body.text: The rate variance threshold is set at 15% because contracted rates can drift due to legitimate reasons such as surcharge pass-throughs, quarterly indexation, or negotiated substitutions that outpace documentation. Recovery history indicates that rate variances under approximately 12% typically do not result in recoverable amounts after review. This justifies setting the threshold slightly higher at 15% to focus on actionable discrepancies.
